items.h: Jefferies downgrades Apple to Underperform on all-glass iPhone cancellation
items.m: Jefferies cut AAPL from Hold to Underperform, pre-market shares fell ~1.3%, citing the scrapped all-glass iPhone and rising memory-cost inflation pressuring margins.

items.h: Apple tests CXMT memory chips to ease supply squeeze
items.m: WSJ reported Apple has held preliminary talks with China's CXMT to source memory chips for iPhones/MacBooks as the AI-driven memory shortage bites; raises US policy concerns over tech transfer.

items.h: Nvidia falls ~2-3% on $500B AI financing plan and Microsoft chip competition
items.m: NVDA shares dropped as investors weighed a reported $500B financing push (with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock's GIP, Brookfield) to fund AI data centers/power, plus concerns Microsoft's in-house Maia 300 chip threatens share; Mark Cuban warned the financing structure could make the market fragile.

items.h: Zuckerberg publishes AI vision essay, launches open-weight Muse Glimmer model
items.m: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a downloadable open-weight agentic model runnable on a single-GPU laptop, alongside a 6,510-word Zuckerberg essay arguing against centralized AI control and for lower US barriers to open-source AI versus Chinese rivals. Stock ended roughly flat.

items.h: Alphabet cloud backlog highlighted after 82% Cloud revenue growth print
items.m: Coverage continued to focus on Alphabet's Google Cloud backlog reaching $514B and 82% cloud revenue growth last quarter, with commentary on whether next quarter's cloud momentum can extend further; stock traded in a $352.71-$357.90 range.

items.h: Micron says demand signals 'exceptional', expects 2027 tighter than 2026
items.m: At the KeyBanc Technology Leadership Forum, Micron executives said AI-driven memory demand is outpacing supply, noted Strategic Customer Agreements now cover roughly half of revenue through 2030, and flagged calendar 2027 as an even tighter supply year than 2026.

items.h: Broadcom shares consolidate near $427 as VMware AI security upgrades support sentiment
items.m: AVGO traded in a $424.50-$432.68 range; bullish commentary continued to cite Broadcom's custom AI accelerator positioning (guided to top $100B in 2027 custom silicon revenue) and recent VMware Cloud Foundation security enhancements (vDefend, Avi Load Balancer).

items.h: Amazon triggers bullish 'Power Inflow' signal, plans Texas natural-gas power plant
items.m: AMZN saw a notable institutional/retail buy-side inflow signal intraday (shares ranged $272.12-$278.31), while separate reporting said Amazon is investing in a natural-gas power plant for a Texas data center even as it maintains climate pledges.

items.h: Oracle rises ~1.5-2% despite ongoing debt-funded AI data-center concerns
items.m: ORCL gained near $149 as dip-buyers returned, even as investors continued to weigh Oracle's negative free cash flow, ~$260B in data-center lease obligations, and the July S&P downgrade to BBB- one notch above speculative grade; Michael Burry's short remains a talking point.
